records.issue_text: [BUG] The signature change of `downsize`/`optimize` from positional `(width, height)` to a single `dimensions` string breaks every pre-existing in-tree caller that still passes two dimension arguments (e.g. animated thumbnail generation and `upload_creator`/`OptimizedImage` call sites that call `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)`). An old caller `downsize(from, to, 100, 100)` now binds `dimensions=100` and `opts=100`; `opts[:allow_animation]` raises TypeError (100[:allow_animation] → no implicit conversion of Symbol into Integer) or produces instructions like `downsize 100` instead of `100x100`, so thumbnail generation of animated/normal images fails with a 500.
records.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb` the diff introduces a *second* `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` which, in Ruby, overwrites the earlier `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` definition. That means any existing callers still using `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height)` will now be interpreted as `dimensions=max_width` and `opts=max_height` (a number), and then `optimize` uses `opts[:allow_animation]` (`def self.optimize(..., dimensions, opts={})`), which will raise when `opts` is not a Hash. This matches the finding’s failure mode and is directly implied

records.issue_text: [BUG] `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same path as ImageMagick's input and output file, which the generated `convert` command cannot handle in place — the instructions are built as `convert <from> ... <to>` and ImageMagick opens/truncates the output before fully consuming certain inputs (notably animated GIFs after `coalesce`). Uploading a large animated GIF that needs downsizing runs `convert /tmp/x.gif ... /tmp/x.gif`; ImageMagick either errors (exitstatus != 0, `downsize` returns false which the caller ignores) or produces a truncated/blank file, which is then passed to `Upload.create_for` and fails or corrupts the upload; the loop can also never reduce size (non-shrinking `80%` of a PNG with large metadata), silently leaving the file oversized after 5 attempts with no error surfaced.
records.rationale: The diff introduces an in-place downsize in `uploads_controller.rb`: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` uses the same file path for input and output. In `optimized_image.rb`, `optimize` ultimately calls `convert_with(instructions, to)` which executes the ImageMagick command (built as a `convert ... <to>`-style instruction sequence) and returns `false` on nonzero exit (`return false if $?.exitstatus != 0`). The new upload loop ignores the return value entirely and will proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` even if the conversion failed or produced a bad/empty file

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The API URL download path hardcodes `10.megabytes` as the download cap, decoupling it from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb`, while the downsizing block below the download only runs `if tempfile && ... && SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`. Admins who set `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB get API URL downloads silently truncated/rejected at 10MB even though their setting allows more; conversely with the setting at 0 (unlimited) a 9MB animated GIF download is never downsized because the guard requires `> 0`, then fails upload creation with a confusing size error.
records.rationale: In `UploadsController#create_upload`, the API URL download limit was changed from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a hardcoded `10.megabytes` (`tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`). This decouples the download cap from the configured `max_image_size_kb`, so instances configured to allow >10MB uploads will still have API URL downloads fail/stop at 10MB. The downsizing block below is also explicitly gated by `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb > 0`, but the key verifiable defect from the diff is the hardcoded 10MB cap ignoring the site setting.

On a site with max_image_size_kb = 2048, a user whose 5MB upload is rejected with 413 is told the limit is 10MB — a factually wrong message that guarantees repeat failed uploads.

records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The downsize loop has no failure verification: after 5 attempts the file may still exceed max_image_size_kb, and each convert_with failure returns false without stopping the loop or being checked. A user uploads a stubbornly large image (e.g. a PNG that resists 80% quality reduction), the loop burns 5 ImageMagick subprocesses, then Upload.create_for is called with an over-limit tempfile anyway — the user gets a raw size error after a multi-second hang instead of a clear 'cannot reduce below limit' message.
records.rationale: The diff adds a new downsizing loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but never checks its return value, and the loop termination condition only inspects `tempfile.size` (`while attempt > 0 && tempfile.size > SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes`). In `optimized_image.rb`, `convert_with` returns `false` on failure, and `optimize` returns that result, but the controller ignores it. Therefore, if downsizing repeatedly fails or doesn’t reduce size below the limit within 5 tries, the code will still proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with an over-limit tempfi
